title: An interpretable machine learning model based on routine clinical indicators for early identification of obesity-related non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in children: a single-center retrospective study.
summary: A single-center retrospective study of 439 children with obesity found that a seven-variable LightGBM model predicted ultrasound-defined fatty liver disease with test AUC 0.870; external validation remains needed.
ai_technology: Six machine-learning models were trained on seven routine clinical variables from 439 children with obesity; LightGBM performed best and SHAP ranked feature contributions.

evidence.tested: In a single-center retrospective cohort, LightGBM predicted ultrasound-defined fatty liver disease with test AUC 0.870, accuracy 0.823, sensitivity 0.787, specificity 0.855 and F1 0.807.
evidence.unknown: Only 439 children from one hospital were studied. External validation and prospective clinical utility before confirmatory ultrasound are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Six machine-learning models were trained on seven routine clinical variables from 439 children with obesity; LightGBM performed best and SHAP ranked feature contributions.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
